extracted.intended_audience: professional photojournalists and documentary photographers considering entry to the World Press Photo Contest
extracted.subtask_description: Call for entries for the 2026 World Press Photo Contest including eligibility requirements, acceptable submission formats (Singles, Stories, Long‑Term Projects), deadline, geographic scope, and prizes. Intended to tell professional photographers how to qualify and what work is welcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — professional photographers
rubrics_metrics.description: The World Press Photo contest is open to professional photographers working in the field of journalism and/or documentary photography.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entrants must be professional; the page specifies that 'Every entrant needs to provide a document with a valid date that confirms their current professional status.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof of professional status — acceptable documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples of documents that confirm current professional status include press card; at least 1 proof of publication (e.g., tearsheet) from 2024 or 2025 with your name visible as credit; journalism union membership card; membership document from a recognized photographic association showing professional membership; a recent letter of reference (must be from 2024 or 2025) from a photo agency, photo editor, media organization or publication stating you have worked for them as a photographer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you are not able to provide proof that meets the above criteria, you may register with alternative (multiple) documents so that organizers can gain a better understanding of your professional status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format-based categories
rubrics_metrics.description: There are three format-based categories: Singles, Stories and Long-Term Projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These categories welcome work that documents news and/or aftermaths, sports, nature, and social, political and environmental issues and solutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject matter and scope of entries
rubrics_metrics.description: The contest awards the best and most compelling photojournalism and documentary photography from the past year; photographers are encouraged to enter images 'whether they capture the wonder of nature or the challenges of the climate crisis, incredible athletic feats, or stories of human resilience and courage.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The contest 'welcomes visual storytelling covering all topics and themes.' Use this guidance to determine whether your work's subject matter is appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadline / Entry period
rubrics_metrics.description: The 2026 World Press Photo Contest is open for entries until 17 January 2026.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure submissions are completed before 01/17/26 (the page shows 'Deadline: 01/17/26').

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No entry fee is required according to the page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic eligibility / Location
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Photographers from around the world are encouraged to enter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awards and benefits for winners
rubrics_metrics.description: Winners will have their work included in the annual World Press Photo touring exhibition, published on the World Press Photo website and social platforms, and included in the World Press Photo Yearbook.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monetary and material prizes include: €1,000 for each of the winners and an additional €10,000 for the World Press Photo of the Year winner; FUJIFILM GFX cameras and lenses awarded to the World Press Photo of the Year winner and two finalists; invitation to a winners' event in Amsterdam for all winners; and a physical award for all winners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation Criteria (stated)
rubrics_metrics.description: The page's 'Evaluation Criteria' section restates the 'General entry rules' — specifically the contest is open to professional photographers and entrants must provide valid dated documentation of professional status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No additional judging metrics (e.g., technical quality, storytelling, ethics) are listed on this page beyond the eligibility/proof requirements and the format/subject welcome statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Considerations / special notes
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page explicitly lists 'Nil' under Considerations, indicating no extra special conditions or caveats are provided in this call announcement.
